photographs.title: Battlefield of Gettysburg. Dead Confederate sharpshooter at foot of Little Round Top
photographs.creator: Gardner, Alexander, 1821-1882
reproduction_numbers: LC-DIG-ppmsca-32920 (digital file from original item)
LC-B171-277 (b&w film copy neg. from similar image with different cropping)
notes_loc: Title from item.
Illus. in:  E468.7 .G19, Gardner's photographic sketch book of the war / Alexander Gardner. Washington, D.C. : Philp & Solomons, [c1866], v. 1, pl. 40.

A clipping from Confederate veterans, v. 33 glued to back of the mount of LOT 4168, no. 19 identifies the soldier depicted as Andrew Johnston Hoge. William Frassanito has shown that while Hoge died at Gettysburg, his regiment was not involved in fighting near Devil's Den during the battle. (See: Early photography at Gettysburg / William Frassanito. Gettysburg : Thomas Publications, 1995, page 277.) Recent scholarship by John Heiser and Scott Fink contends that the soldier was likely part of the 2nd or 15th Georgia Infantry.
Photographer and date from image in Gardner's Photographic Sketch Book.
Hand written on verso: "Same as Miller  vol. II, p. 249".
Gift; Col. Godwin Ordway; 1948.

notes_loc: A clipping from Confederate veterans, v. 33 glued to back of the mount of LOT 4168, no. 19 identifies the soldier depicted as Andrew Johnston Hoge. William Frassanito has shown that while Hoge died at Gettysburg, his regiment was not involved in fighting near Devil's Den during the battle. (See: Early photography at Gettysburg / William Frassanito. Gettysburg : Thomas Publications, 1995, page 277.) Recent scholarship by John Heiser and Scott Fink contends that the soldier was likely part of the 2nd or 15th Georgia Infantry.

This photograph is titled "The home of a Rebel Sharpshooter, Gettysburg" In Alexander Gardner's Photographic Sketch Book of the Civil War (Reprint; New York : Dover Publications, Inc. 1959), plate 41.
While Gardner is credited as the photographer in his "Sketchbook," his original catalogue (published Sept. 1863) credits Timothy O'Sullivan as the photographer.

notes_loc: Photographer name on negative sleeve: Gardner.

Each of these glass negatives is a "copy" of one half of an original stereograph glass negative. (See neg. LC-B815-251.) The copy negative numbers are: LC-B811-251A, LC-B811-251B, and LC-B811-251C. The number "942" is on variant A; "251" is on variant B; and "942" is on variant C.

William Frassanito in "Gettysburg: A Journey in Time" credits Timothy O'Sullivan as the photographer of this image. "Although Gardner claimed credit for this view in his "Sketch Book," the original catalogue issued only two months following the battle identified the cameraman as O'Sullivan."

Published in: Published in: Gardner, Alexander / Gardner's photographic sketch book of the War. Washington, D.C. : Philp & Solomons [1865], plate 41, with the title "Home of a rebel sharpshooter, Gettysburg."

A clipping from Confederate veterans, v. 33 glued to back of the mount of LOT 4168, no. 19 identifies the soldier depicted as Andrew Johnston Hoge. William Frassanito has shown that while Hoge died at Gettysburg, his regiment was not involved in fighting near Devil's Den during the battle. (See: Early photography at Gettysburg / William Frassanito. Gettysburg : Thomas Publications, 1995, page 277.) Recent scholarship by John Heiser and Scott Fink contends that the soldier was likely part of the 2nd or 15th Georgia Infantry.

photographs.creator: O'Sullivan, Timothy H., 1840-1882
reproduction_numbers: LC-DIG-cwpb-00073 (digital file from original neg.)
notes_loc: Title from Civil War caption books.
Caption from negative sleeve: Rocks could not save him at the Battle of Gettysburg. July 1863.
Published in: Gardner, Alexander / Gardner's photographic sketch book of the War. Washington, D.C. : Philp & Solomons [1865], plate 41, with the title "Home of a rebel sharpshooter, Gettysburg."

William Frassanito in "Gettysburg: A Journey in Time" credits Timothy O'Sullivan as the photographer of this image. "Although Gardner claimed credit for this view in his "Sketch Book," the original catalogue issued only two months following the battle identified the cameraman as O'Sullivan."
Library also has single-frame glass copy negatives for this image with the call number LC-B811-251.

A clipping from Confederate veterans, v. 33 glued to back of the mount of LOT 4168, no. 19 identifies the soldier depicted as Andrew Johnston Hoge. William Frassanito has shown that while Hoge died at Gettysburg, his regiment was not involved in fighting near Devil's Den during the battle. (See: Early photography at Gettysburg / William Frassanito. Gettysburg : Thomas Publications, 1995, page 277.) Recent scholarship by John Heiser and Scott Fink contends that the soldier was likely part of the 2nd or 15th Georgia Infantry.
